issues.description: Class 'Lecture' in the solution declares instance fields using snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the constructor and accessor methods reference camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). This naming mismatch appears in the solution file and contradicts the UML and attribute names used in the problem statement, and will cause compilation errors because the constructor and methods refer to undeclared fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier names consistent. Rename the declared instance fields in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to camelCase to match the UML and the rest of the implementation: lecture_name -> lectureName, number_of_inscribed_students -> numberOfInscribedStudents, number_of_guest_students -> numberOfGuestStudents, number_of_lecturers -> numberOfLecturers, number_of_tutors -> numberOfTutors. Alternatively (less preferable) update the constructor parameter names and all method references to use the snake_case field names, but prefer following the UML and Java naming conventions (camelCase) so the template, problem statement, and solution align and compile.
